dct_description_sm: Kilpisjrvi Biological Station is situated in the mountain birch forest zone near the 70th degree of northern latitude (6903'N; 2050'E) in the northwestern part of Finland. Station belongs to University of Helsinki, the Faculty of Biological and Environmental sciences. Long-term follow-up studies form the core of the research activities at the station. The most long-lasting series of observations concern variations in the numbers of small rodents over a 50-year period. The Population dynamics of passerine birds have been monitored since 1957. Long-term research projects also include periodicity in the quality and quantity of vegetation in the mountain region, and the connection between these phenomena and variation in all animal populations. Current follow-up research topics include the nesting habits of the rough-legged buzzard (Buteo lagopus), the birch (Betula pubescens ssp. czerepanovii) seed crop, the production of fungi, fish stocks in Lake Kilpisjrvi and the influence of the snow cover on vegetation.
dct_title_s: Population dynamics of hole-nesting passerine birds in Lapland, Finland
